all_segments.text: Nike made this shoe to control your mind. Well, not exactly. Let me explain.
This wildly futuristic piece of footwear is called the Nike Mind 001,
and it was developed by Nike's Mind Science Department, who apparently not only love creating wild-looking pieces of footwear,
but also shoes that look like the Cybertruck. That's all I can see when I look at this shoe.
I see Cybertruck, especially the silver one. But the whole idea behind this piece of footwear
is to activate different sensory parts of your brain through your feet.
And what these shoes are meant to do is help you focus and calm down and be more connected with your surroundings.
And so in order to test this, I got as stressed out as I possibly could and then tried the font for the first time.
All right, so I don't know what to expect with these. I don't know if they're going to be, like, game-changing
or if they're going to be mind-controlling. I have no idea. So why don't we throw these guys on feet
and see if Nike's got a winner on their hands? It feels pretty normal.
You know, I feel like some, I guess, dimples or bumps.
But here we go. Let's try it out. First time standing in the... They're not bad.
Maybe it's because I'm on carpet. Like, I don't really feel them. They're not really pressing into my feet that much.
They're definitely comfortable. Hold on. Let me try them over here. But there's some hardwood floor.
In the corner. Oh, yeah. You're definitely feeling more on the hardwood floor.
I'm sorry. This is the only place there's hardwood floor in the studio.
It's not as aggressive as I was expecting. I was expecting, like, everything I was hearing
from people talking online was, like, it feels like foot reflexology. Maybe not that intense.
But, like, you feel it and you notice what's going on. This kind of feels like bigger versions of Crocs,
a larger Crocs nub on the bottom of your foot.
I mean, maybe I haven't worn these long enough. I plan to wear them all day and see what happens. I'm disappointed to say that
because I was really hoping for, like, this ground-shattering experience. I didn't even want, like, a nice soft underfoot feel.
I wanted a feel that, like, made me think, wow, I'm so, like, relieved right now.
I'm so unstressed. I'm still just as stressed as I was five minutes ago.
See, that's strange, though. I'm starting to feel a bit calmer.
I'm sitting and I haven't been able to sit all day? Or is that because of the shoes?
All right, since trying these on for the first time, I have been wearing these around throughout the day
and they are better than I expected, but we'll get into that. There's a few things about this shoe
that have captured people's attention and helped it go viral and completely sell out.
The first is obviously the aesthetic. This nodule traction pattern thing
going on in the outsole of the shoe is very, very different. And the fact that it moves and flexes,
depending on how you're walking, gives it an even more organic, futuristic,
almost alien look. But not only does this shoe promise to give you a very unique look,
but it also promises to make you more focused and make you feel more connected with your surroundings,
which is definitely something wild, especially when it's apparently supposed to interact with your brain
in a way that no other piece of footwear ever has. So needless to say,
when the launch date for this shoe was finally announced as January 8th
for a retail price of $95, yeah, I lined up digitally
on DickSportingGoods.com and had it shipped to my house.
I didn't actually physically line up anywhere. I'm not an athlete. I'm not who this shoe is for,
but I still bought it like you probably did. And the hype levels for this mule are off the charts
because I think the three colorways that dropped on January 8th, which at the time I'm filming this video is today,
completely sold out, like entirely. And I think it's because people are really interested
to find out whether this shoe actually lives up to the hype. And so by the end of the video,
you're going to know whether I think this shoe lives up to the hype or whether I think it's just another gimmick.
Of course, if you don't want to watch the review and try this shoe out for yourself, or maybe you just want to grab a pair for yourself
because you like the way it looks, I've made sure to link it through the YouTube shopping tab on your screen
at places like StockX and all the different colorways. The one colorway that I really wanted,
the black one, unfortunately hasn't released yet. I think it releases in February
for the same retail price of $95. And of course, there is the Mind002,
which is a sneaker, which as weird as this looks, it actually still looks better than the sneaker version.
I don't think this design is supposed to be a sneaker. I don't think it looks good as a sneaker.
That said though, the sneaker does still feature the same technology. So you've got two different ways
to try out this Nike Mind tech. So surprisingly, this $95 pair of mules
does not come in the standard Nike orange box. Instead, it comes in a white box
with Nike Mind branding all over it. On the top, you've got the foot hotspots
or the areas that apparently the nodes are pressing against your foot
and activating your brain. The graphic in the box though, which is probably the extent of my knowledge
on this topic, looks good. Inside the box, the paper comes with the same design
in black and gray. And of course, both of these shoes come with little hang tags.
One says that these are not made for zero to three-year-olds, which is odd.
I don't know if it's because it's a choking hazard if one of these nodes fall off, or maybe it would explode their brains.
I'm genuinely nervous at letting my below three-year-old child try these. And I don't know why.
It doesn't even say. It just has a little picture of like, no toddlers, please. Maybe it's because of those.
It's probably because of those. But that's pretty much all you get inside the box. Then you get to the shoes themselves,
and man, they are different. First of all, the upper, and I guess a majority of the shoes
come in this pretty standard feeling Nike foam.
I call it Nike foam because it's foam made by Nike, but realistically it feels like really all the foam
used on foam slides and Crocs and foam runners and things like that.
It's soft, it's flexible, but it's nothing new. The design of this mule is sort of split up
into two different halves with this chamfer that runs all the way through the shoe. The top half comes in this smooth matte finish.
The bottom half comes in this almost like cookie cutter ribbed design
with these perforated, or I guess semi-perforated because they don't go all the way through,
kind of dot pattern patterns. Now the ridges along the side of the shoe,
I'll be honest, I don't love. They're obviously there though to mimic the shape of the nodes
and kind of show where the nodes sit along the sides of the shoe and make them look kind of like pistons
that articulate underneath your feet, which is essentially what they are.
I'm fine with that, but I'll be honest, the toe of the sneaker looks a little cookie cutter-ish.
You know what I mean? Like literally cut by a cookie cutter, which is not a bad thing,
but it's not personally my taste. But one thing that I think is important to note about these,
or at least that I'm taking away from these, is that I don't believe these are designed to be worn day-to-day.
Like everyday, all-day shoes. I think these are the kind of shoes that you wear around the house,
maybe to the gym before you go play ball. Maybe if you lift in these or something,
I don't know if you're supposed to do that, but maybe that's what you do before you play ball. These are more of a recovery shoe,
or I guess pre-exercise shoe than anything else. It's not supposed to replace your pair of Vans or your running sneakers.
I would assume you shouldn't run in these. That's my guess. I don't run in mules in general, not even my own mules.
I just, it's just not worth it. One thing that I found interesting about this shoe that I didn't even know about until I actually got this in hand
is that this center area right there on the top of, I guess your foot, kind of like a tongue area,
it's not actually foam all the way through. You can sort of see on the inside of the shoe,
the foam is kind of cut in this U shape, almost in like a smaller version of the shape you see up here on the top of the shoe.
That area instead is this sort of shiny fabric material that's very thin, but it is perforated,
so it helps with breathability. You've got a Nike logo there in the center, but it kind of collapses in a weird way.
And I do find that, I don't know if it like sits on my foot in a weird way or what it is,
but like my left pinky toe kind of like clicks in a weird way.
My feet like click a lot. I have a lot of like weird joints in my feet, but like whatever way that my pinky toe sits in this shoe,
it kind of like, it's not uncomfortable, but it's a weird way for it to be positioned.
So it's something that I probably have to get used to, but that's because I think of the shape of the inside of the top of the shoe.
The foam gets very thick and then just all of a sudden disappears, and then you've got this fabric material,
and then it gets very thick again. You don't really feel that too much on the top of your foot,
but maybe you do. I don't know. Let me, hold on. I don't think it's not giving my foot room to move.
Like, I don't know exactly what's going on in there, but something's up. Maybe it's always happened,
and my mind is so focused while wearing this shoe that I'm just noticing it for the first time.
Who knows? Either way, that's probably not something you're gonna have to deal with. That's, I'm sure, just a me problem.
One of the standout details on the shoe, and a detail that I really, really like for whatever reason,
is the Nike logo is placed vertically on the lateral side of the shoe
in this sort of, I guess, metallic silver kind of color. On the medial side, you don't have that.
You do have the Nike logo, but instead it's pressed into the shoe, or I guess indented into the shoe,
along with this perforated pattern like you have on the other side, and these ventilation holes,
which you don't have on the other side. They're only on the medial side for that added breathability,
which is nice. I mean, I'll be honest with you. I don't think mules are ever not breathable,
just because the nature of the shoe, the whole back of the shoe is missing, so realistically, air gets in, whether you like it or not.
So I don't feel like it's super necessary, but that's just me.
But that's pretty much all you've got around the outside of the upper. You do have this glossy Nike logo right there on the heel,
which, is that Nike Nectar, that 3D-printed technology that they used on the Nike Air Max 95000s?
I don't know. It kind of looks similar to the Nike tags on the Nike Air Max 95000s.
I'm not totally sure. I wouldn't be surprised if it was or if it wasn't. Now, moving inside the shoe,
you get to one of the most interesting-looking parts of the entire shoe, and that is, of course, this fabric insole,
